openClinicalQuestions: Which amenorrhoea threshold should WHD use in India-facing copy when NHS (3 missed periods) and other guidelines differ?
Should adolescent-specific cycle cut-offs from the PCOS/PMOS guideline be cross-linked more prominently from this page?

claimLedger.claim: Normal menstrual frequency described as predictable cyclic menses every 24–38 days; regularity uses shortest-to-longest variation of about 7–9 days by age band.
claimLedger.sourceSection: FIGO · The two FIGO systems for normal and abnormal uterine bleeding symptoms… (2018 revisions) · 2018 (page correction note 12 November 2018)
claimLedger.limitations: International nomenclature system; public UK NHS cut-offs (21/35 days) differ and are also cited for patient-facing simplicity.

claimLedger.claim: Irregular if gap <21 or >35 days; more likely at puberty and near menopause; see a GP for irregular periods, >7-day bleeds, intermenstrual bleeding, associated symptoms, or difficulty conceiving.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Irregular periods · not stated on fetched page header
claimLedger.limitations: UK primary-care advice; Indian access routes and specialist timing may differ.

claimLedger.claim: See a GP if you have missed your period 3 times in a row (among other prompts); lists pregnancy, breastfeeding, contraception, PMOS/PCOS, menopause and other causes.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Missed or late periods · not stated on fetched page header
claimLedger.limitations: Open clinical question for India: local clinics may use different amenorrhoea thresholds; article attributes the 3-missed-period prompt to NHS.

claimLedger.claim: Seek advice for symptom combinations if you might be pregnant even without a positive test; emergency care for sudden intense tummy pain with dizziness/fainting.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Ectopic pregnancy — Overview · Page last reviewed: 23 August 2022
claimLedger.limitations: UK emergency numbers; readers in India should use local emergency services.
